results.name: unanimous_cell_fraction
results.description: Fraction of (set, target) cells with >=5 responses where all responses agree (all yes or all no); observed > null means human judgments are more extreme/deterministic per item than the model's graded probabilities predict (model too lukewarm), observed < null means the reverse.

results.name: trial_index_drift
results.description: Pearson correlation between trial_index and the yes response across all trials; observed above (below) null means people drift toward saying yes (no) later in the session, a drift the stationary model cannot produce.

results.name: first_vs_last_example_digit_match
results.description: Among multi-example sets whose first and last shown examples have different final digits, yes-rate for targets sharing the first example's final digit (but not the last's) minus yes-rate for targets sharing the last's (but not the first's); nonzero observed vs a ~0 null means people weight examples by presentation order, which the order-blind model cannot do (positive = primacy, negative = recency).
results.code:
# name: first_vs_last_example_digit_match
# description: Among multi-example sets whose first and last shown examples have different final digits, yes-rate for targets sharing the first example's final digit (but not the last's) minus yes-rate for targets sharing the last's (but not the first's); nonzero observed vs a ~0 null means people weight examples by presentation order, which the order-blind model cannot do (positive = primacy, negative = recency).
def test_statistic(df):
    parts = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    n = parts.str.len()
    f = parts.str[0].astype(int) % 10
    l = parts.str[-1].astype(int) % 10
    td = df["target"].astype(int) % 10
    base = (n >= 2) & (f != l)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    a = r[base & (td == f)]
    b = r[base & (td == l)]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: gcd2_even_nondigit_yes_rate
results.description: Among multi-example all-even sets whose gcd is exactly 2, yes-rate for even targets whose final digit matches no example; observed > null means the model (no "even numbers" rule, mutual-similarity penalty) under-generalises to the even-number concept.

results.name: target_is_example_excess
results.description: Yes-rate for targets identical to one of the shown examples minus yes-rate for other targets that share an example's final digit; observed > null means the model under-credits exact repeats of an example (it only sees the shared final digit).

results.name: math_category_target_boost
results.description: Among sets of >=2 examples that all lie in a named category (powers of 2, perfect squares, or cubes), yes-rate for non-example targets in that category minus yes-rate for non-example targets outside it; observed > null means the model (no such concepts) under-generalises to category members.

results.name: single_example_fine_proximity
results.description: For single-example sets and targets not sharing the example's final digit, yes-rate for targets within 10 of the example minus yes-rate for targets more than 40 away; observed > null means the model's coarse decade-band familiarity under-represents fine numerical-magnitude similarity.
results.code:
# name: single_example_fine_proximity
# description: For single-example sets and targets not sharing the example's final digit, yes-rate for targets within 10 of the example minus yes-rate for targets more than 40 away; observed > null means the model's coarse decade-band familiarity under-represents fine numerical-magnitude similarity.
def test_statistic(df):
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    single = ~ns.str.contains(",")
    x = pd.to_numeric(ns.where(single, "0"), errors="coerce").fillna(0).astype(int)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    d = (t - x).abs()
    base = single & ((t % 10) != (x % 10))
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    a = r[base & (d <= 10)]
    b = r[base & (d > 40)]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())
